runs.best_epoch_note: INHERITED from the dicos-p6 parent; no epoch of this run beat it
runs.finding: PATIENCE CANNOT BE A CONSTANT. Patience 6 counted staleness against an inherited best reached at the end of an anneal, at learning rate 1e-6. Restarting the scheduler to peak makes the model worse by construction before it can be better, so the counter was already spent before the run had a chance. The trajectory was still descending monotonically from epoch 19 when it stopped. This is a statement about the stopping rule, not about the model.
runs.remedy: patience must equal the run horizon when resuming from an annealed best; dicos-p9 and dicos-p10 use patience 24 for 24 epochs

runs.resumed_from: the dicos-p6 epoch-15 BEST checkpoint, on both the resume_from and resume_best_from slots
runs.wall_minus_epoch_note: dataset construction plus 24 per-epoch visualization exports
runs.finding: CONTINUING A SPENT COSINE BEATS RESTARTING IT. CosineAnnealingLR is periodic in 2*T_max, so a scheduler resumed past its first anneal climbs smoothly back toward peak and re-anneals, SGDR-like, without extra machinery. p9 differed from p8 in exactly two declared settings -- restart_scheduler_on_resume false, and patience widened to the full horizon -- and improved 0.067238 where p8 improved nothing over the same nominal 24-epoch request.
